newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: More than 300,000 join Serb church protest march.
newsitem.headline: More than 300,000 join Serb church protest march.

text.p: More than 300,000 people filed solemnly through central Belgrade on Monday in a march called by the powerful Serbian Orthodox church to protest against election fraud, witnesses said.
Patriarch Pavle, who is in his 80s, led the procession flanked by about 20 priests chanting Orthodox hymns and carrying a banner of Saint Sava, on whose holy day the march was held.

The witnesses said the march, which swelled rapidly in size, began at 7:30 a.m. (0630 GMT) at the Serbian Orthodox Cathedral and made its way quietly through sunny, early morning streets towards the Saint Sava Temple about 3 km (two miles) away.
The protest was the biggest since half a million people turned out on to the streets for the Orthodox New Year on January 14.
Police, who have clubbed demonstrators in recent days as the pro-democracy protests have dragged into a 10th week, kept their distance.
Earlier, police withdrew a cordon blocking student pro-democracy demonstrators who had held a non-stop rally for eight days in a test of will with the authorities.
Some 50,000 students and supporters then swept triumphantly through the city in a boisterous, whistle-blowing march in the pre-dawn hours.
The students later linked up with the church procession and student organisers served as orderlies for crowd control while traffic policemen looked on.

The church's involvement stepped up the pressure on the government of Socialist President Slobodan Milosevic to acknowledge victories by the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition in municipal elections last November.
The opposition victories in 14 cities, including the capital Belgrade, were annulled by the government, but Milosevic has been under strong pressure from the West to reinstate them.
